description.narrative:
This project has the socio-environmental education aim to disseminate among the local population and church leaders in the region and dioceses, alternative, sustainable sources of energy contributing to raising awareness on climate change and the impacts of the current model of generating energy. In Rondônia State, the construction of three major dams and hydro-electric power stations have caused huge social and environmental impacts. More dams are on the planning stage for Rondônia, including a major bi-national dam between Brazil and Bolivia, highly criticised due to its immediate and future socio environmental impact in the area.
This demonstrative project aims to install solar system producing clean, renewable and sustainable energy in a regional seminary serving 4 dioceses (Guajara-Mirim-ro, Lábrea-AM, Humaitá-AM and Porto Velho-Rondônia). The reason to choose the seminary was to give an educational purpose to the project to raise awareness among students, their families, local catholic communities and the local population through a concrete example of solar energy production and the benefit of generating alternative energy and connecting it to the main electricity grid. This initiative also aims to provide information and arguments for church leaders, community activists and environmentalists to continue lobbying the Brazilian government to change the current energy matrix and policy, based on the construction of mega dams that bring huge socio-environmental impacts. This small project has also the potential to promote among the local population the use of the current legislation which allows decentralised generation of alternative energy to be connected to the main grid, showing that a change in the policy is doable/viable.
